title: Finite normalization and DVR branches of a reduced Nagata curve ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a reduced commutative local Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Reduced means that $a^n=0$, $n\geq1$, implies $a=0$, and local means that $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal. For any ring $T$, write $Q(T)=S_T^{-1}T$, where $S_T$ consists of the non-zero-divisors $s$ (those satisfying $sx=0\Rightarrow x=0$). Let $B\subset Q(A)$ be the integral closure of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $A$ has finitely many minimal prime ideals $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$. Put $D_i=A/\mathfrak p_i$ and $K_i=A_{\mathfrak p_i}$, with localization at a prime as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Each $D_i$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local Nagata domain, and the canonical map identifies $K_i$ with its fraction field. Here a domain is a nonzero ring without zero divisors, and Noetherian is as in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $E_i\subset K_i$ be the integral closure of $D_i$. Each $E_i$ is finite as a $D_i$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and is a Dedekind domain, meaning a Noetherian domain of dimension $1$ integrally closed in its fraction field. The canonical isomorphism $Q(A)\cong\prod_iK_i$ identifies $B$ with $\prod_iE_i$, and $B$ is finite as an $A$-module. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$, there is a unique factor $E_i$ and a nonzero maximal prime $\mathfrak r\subset E_i$ over $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p_i$ such that the canonical localization isomorphism is $B_{\mathfrak q}\cong(E_i)_{\mathfrak r}$. In particular every such $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

source.place: Tags 0C3S (lemma-pre-delta-invariant) and 0C3V (lemma-normalization-same-after-completion), component normalization and local DVR input; no completion conclusion.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], $A$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] to enumerate its distinct minimal primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$. None equals $\mathfrak m$: if the unique maximal ideal were minimal, every prime, being contained in it, would equal it, contrary to $\dim A=1$. For each $i$, $D_i=A/\mathfrak p_i$ is a nonzero domain, and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. Ideals of $D_i$ correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $\mathfrak p_i$, by inverse image and $J\mapsto J/\mathfrak p_i$; these operations preserve and reflect primality and inclusion. Thus $D_i$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p_i$, and has dimension exactly one: $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p_i$ is a prime chain and any longer chain would lift to one in $A$. For every prime $\mathfrak a/\mathfrak p_i$ of $D_i$, its quotient is $A/\mathfrak a$, which is N-2 by the Nagata hypothesis. This and Noetherianity verify directly that $D_i$ is Nagata.

source.place: Tags 032R (definition-nagata), 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), and 00KE (definition-Krull); quotient ideal correspondence written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] to $A$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $Q(A)\simeq\prod_iK_i$, each $K_i$ a field with $\mathfrak p_iK_i=0$. The kernel of $A\to K_i$ is exactly $\mathfrak p_i$: elements of that ideal vanish, while every element outside it becomes a unit in this nonzero field. Thus $D_i\hookrightarrow K_i$. Every element of $K_i=A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ is $a/s$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p_i$, hence is the quotient of the images of $\bar a,\bar s\in D_i$ with $\bar s\ne0$. This identifies $K_i$ canonically with $\operatorname{Frac}(D_i)$.

For each $i$, [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] applied to the prime $\mathfrak p_i$ says that $D_i$ is N-2. Specialize [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] to the degree-one field extension $K_i/K_i$: its integral closure $E_i$ is finite over $D_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], $E_i$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] with base $D_i$ and $F=L=K_i$: $E_i$ is an integrally closed domain with fraction field $K_i$. Its inclusion $D_i\hookrightarrow E_i$ is injective and integral, by the definition of integral closure, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] gives $\dim E_i=\dim D_i=1$. These are precisely the stated Dedekind properties.

Under Step 2, an element of $B$ gives a tuple $(x_i)$ with $x_i\in E_i$: project a monic equation over $A$ to $K_i$, where its coefficients map through $D_i$. Conversely, for $(x_i)\in\prod_iE_i$, choose a monic equation $f_i(x_i)=0$ with $f_i\in D_i[T]$, and lift all coefficients to a monic $\widetilde f_i\in A[T]$. The monic polynomial $F=\prod_i\widetilde f_i$ annihilates $(x_i)$, since in coordinate $i$ its $i$-th factor vanishes. Thus the tuple is integral over $A$. Both implications use only [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and prove that the canonical isomorphism restricts to $B\simeq\prod_iE_i$.

source.place: Tags 00GI (definition-integral), 00GP (definition-integral-closure); coordinatewise monic-equation argument for the component normalization used in varieties.tex Tag 0C3S (lemma-pre-delta-invariant).

proof.text: For each $i$ take finitely many $D_i$-module generators $e_{ij}$ of $E_i$. Embed each $e_{ij}$ as the tuple supported only in factor $i$. These finitely many tuples generate $\prod_iE_i$ over $A$: express each coordinate in its chosen generators, lift its coefficients from $D_i=A/\mathfrak p_i$ to $A$, and sum the resulting supported tuples. By Step 4 they therefore generate $B$, proving that $B$ is finite over $A$.

proof.text:
Identify $B$ with $\prod_iE_i$ and let $e_i$ be the tuple equal to $1$ in factor $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Since $\sum_i e_i=1$, at least one $e_i$ is outside the proper prime $\mathfrak q$. At most one is outside: $e_ie_j=0\in\mathfrak q$ for $i
e j$. For this unique $i$, every $e_j$ with $j
e i$ belongs to $\mathfrak q$, so the kernel of the projection $\pi_i:B	o E_i$ lies in $\mathfrak q$. Put $\mathfrak r=\pi_i(\mathfrak q)$; the quotient $B/\mathfrak q\simeq E_i/\mathfrak r$ shows that $\mathfrak r$ is prime and $\mathfrak q=\pi_i^{-1}(\mathfrak r)$. Its contraction to $D_i$ is $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p_i$ because $\mathfrak q\cap A=\mathfrak m$. The fraction map $b/s\mapsto b_i/s_i$ defines $B_{\mathfrak q}	o(E_i)_{\mathfrak r}$, since $s
otin\mathfrak q$ iff $s_i
otin\mathfrak r$. In $B_{\mathfrak q}$ the idempotent $e_i$ is a unit, hence equals $1$, and $1-e_i=0$. The map $E_i	o B_{\mathfrak q}$ sending $x$ to its supported tuple divided by $1$ is therefore unital; it sends every $x
otin\mathfrak r$ to a unit. It extends to $(E_i)_{\mathfrak r}$, and the two fraction maps are inverse because all other coordinates vanish. This proves the canonical localization isomorphism and uniqueness of its factor and prime.

proof.text: The inclusion $D_i\hookrightarrow E_i$ is integral. Since $\mathfrak r\cap D_i=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p_i$ is maximal, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] makes $\mathfrak r$ maximal. Moreover $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p_i\ne0$ by Step 1, and $D_i\hookrightarrow E_i$ is injective, so $\mathfrak r\ne0$. Apply [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] to the Dedekind domain $E_i$ of Step 3 and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak r$. It gives that $(E_i)_{\mathfrak r}$, and hence the canonically isomorphic $B_{\mathfrak q}$ of Step 6, is a discrete valuation ring.

The contraction of r is m/p_i, and I checked that both fraction maps are well defined and inverse to each other. Uniqueness holds because e_i maps to 0 in every other factor. Step 7: r is maximal by the integral-over-maximal node and nonzero because m/p_i is nonzero, so the Dedekind localization node gives a DVR. Steps 4-6 are genuinely elementary.
